extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: Observation services are specific, clinically appropriate, outpatient services provided to help a healthcare professional decide whether a patient needs to be admitted as an inpatient or can be discharged. This policy outlines the criteria that Humana plans use to determine appropriate billing and documentation of facility observation services.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.subsection: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: References > Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. The following policy applies to facility services only. For Humana Medicaid plans, this policy applies except when not permissible by state Medicaid guidelines.

extracted_content.title: Billing of Observation Services
extracted_content.content: The billing of facility observation services is appropriate only when the observation services were medically necessary, the observation services were ordered by a qualified healthcare professional, the patient was under the care of a physician or qualified nonphysician practitioner during observation services, and one or more of the following is true of the encounter:

extracted_content.title: Billing of Observation Services
extracted_content.content: Treatment and monitoring were provided to determine if inpatient admission was needed

extracted_content.title: Billing of Observation Services
extracted_content.content: The observation services were provided for patient monitoring, after outpatient surgery or diagnostic testing, that was beyond the standard recovery period for the service

extracted_content.title: Billing of Observation Services
extracted_content.content: A qualified healthcare professional directly referred the patient to the facility for observation services

extracted_content.title: Billing of Observation Services
extracted_content.content: The patient was a child who was observed because of an uncertain clinical response to outpatient therapy

extracted_content.title: Billing of Observation Services
extracted_content.content: The patient was a child whose parent or caregiver was unavailable or unknown If none of those events occurred, a Humana plan does not reimburse for a facility observation charge. The billing of and reimbursement for observation services are limited to rendered observation services that were specifically medically necessary and typically do not exceed 48 hours. Any time for any of the following scenarios is excluded from the calculation of billable observation hours:

extracted_content.title: Billing of Observation Services
extracted_content.content: Patient monitoring during diagnostic or therapeutic services, including observation care interrupted by such services

extracted_content.title: Billing of Observation Services
extracted_content.content: Routine preparation for outpatient surgery and diagnostic testing

extracted_content.title: Billing of Observation Services
extracted_content.content: Services provided during the standard recovery period after outpatient surgery, which is four to six hours, or after diagnostic testing

extracted_content.title: Billing of Observation Services
extracted_content.content: Services provided for the convenience of the patient, physician or qualified nonphysician practitioner

extracted_content.hierarchy_path: References > Observation services provided according to a standing order
extracted_content.content: The time period between observation services ending and the arrival of the patient's transportation

extracted_content.title: Documentation of Observation Services
extracted_content.content: Humana reserves the right to request medical records, at any time, to confirm accurate billing of observation services. Medical record documentation for observation services must include:

extracted_content.title: Documentation of Observation Services
extracted_content.content: The physician's or qualified nonphysician practitioner's assessment that determined the patient would benefit from observation services

extracted_content.title: The start and stop times of observation services
extracted_content.subsection: The start and stop times of observation services
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: References > The start and stop times of observation services
extracted_content.content: Time for non-observation services that interrupted observation care, if any

extracted_content.title: Nurses' notes
extracted_content.content: Progress notes on the patient's condition and treatment to confirm the continuing need for observation services

extracted_content.title: Definitions of Italicized Terms
extracted_content.content: Qualified healthcare professional: A physician or another individual authorized by state licensure law and hospital staff bylaws to admit patients to the hospital or to order outpatient tests.
